A1.justification: Both complete 30-page PDFs describe the same TIS-DPO work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–K are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original alignment and summarization experiments in Section 7, plus computational-budget, robustness, sensitivity, token-weight, and UltraFeedback results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments and results in Section 7 and the appendices, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and robustness analyses.

M1.justification: The TIS-DPO objective, weight estimation, clamping, and three contrastive-model construction methods remain unchanged. The position-dependent weight decay in Appendix K was already present in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions use PKU-SafeRLHF, Anthropic-HH, TL;DR, and UltraFeedback. The AdvBench/JailbreakBench, Alpaca, and MT-bench evaluation coverage and the appendix test scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DPO, PPO, IPO, TDPO, and KTO. The RLCD comparison in Table 2, SFT comparison in Figure 3, and reversed-DPO comparison in Table 7 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Model configurations, evaluation metrics and prompts, training hyperparameters, and testing procedures match. The equivalent-compute comparison, 20% annotation-noise condition, sensitivity ranges, and decay setting in the appendices are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 7.5 and Appendices D, F–I, and K retain the same weight and eta ablations, training analysis, case studies, compute comparison, noise test, sensitivity study, token-consistency evaluation, and positional-bias analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Point-estimate reporting and the absence of experimental uncertainty estimates remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 and the plotted and qualitative findings retain the same results. For example, TIS-DPO(D)'s LLaMA2-7B PKU-SafeRLHF safety rate remains 96.7%, and its UltraFeedback win rate remains 69.2%.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2, Definition 1, mathematical objectives, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. The differences in equation size and delimiter rendering are typesetting changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about optimal token-reward distributions, importance sampling, three contrastive estimators, and alignment and summarization improvements. The added code statement does not revise the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning prompt/data-distribution mismatch, contrastive-model effectiveness, computational overhead, missing ground-truth token weights, and positional bias are retained. No substantive interpretation or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: The v3 abstract newly states that code is available and supplies the TIS-DPO GitHub address; v2 lacks this implementation-access pointer. Hardware, hyperparameters, training details, and evaluation prompts otherwise match.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to DPO, TDPO, token-aware data construction, and importance sampling. Reference reflow and hyperlink formatting do not change research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract gains a short code-availability sentence, and the arXiv version/date text updates. The remaining prose and section organization are retained, without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 adjusts equation sizing, compacts Tables 1–2, slightly resizes Figure 3, and changes citation and cross-reference colors to blue. Paragraphs and acknowledgments reflow across pages; no figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 adds a direct implementation-access pointer absent from v2, modestly improving practical usability. Presentation refinements are limited, and the scientific evidence, proofs, and limitations remain unchanged. The PDFs establish improved access information but do not verify the repository's contents.
